name: TDC ADMET PPBR_AZ
description: Predict the percentage of a compound that is bound to proteins in blood plasma from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint PPBR_AZ of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the mean absolute error on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; lower is better.
contract: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: the predicted value. train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the mean absolute error on the test part, minimized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet
Predicts the percentage of a compound bound to plasma proteins (an AstraZeneca assay; 1,797 compounds on the benchmark-group page) from SMILES strings, scored by mean absolute error.
Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
One evaluation of the starting program took 460 s in the run of 2026-11-11, more than the arena's default limit of 120 s: raise AR_EVAL_TIMEOUT for this task.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the percentage of a drug that is bound to plasma proteins (the plasma protein binding rate) from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Only unbound drug is free to reach its target and to be cleared, so the plasma protein binding rate affects dosing and efficacy.
